haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both return 401 with the login page saying "Invalid email or password" and no cookie change. Bcrypt also runs against a dummy hash, so timing matches.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with Retry-After set to seconds remaining, and the page says "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." The password is never checked.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session is deleted in the same transaction as the new session creation, whether or not it belongs to the same user. The browser gets a new sid cookie.
haiku-low.q4: Only the opaque session ID, a 32-byte random base64url value. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It also has Secure, SameSite=Lax and Max-Age=43200.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from login, even with constant use. The expires_at value is set once at login and never extended. The 30-minute idle rule still applies separately.
haiku-low.q6: It returns 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie. An unknown, idle or expired ID gets the same response, as does a request with no cookie.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the matching session row before replying. If the session is already gone, the reply is identical: expired sid cookie and 303 to /login. A delete failure gives 503 and keeps the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the session ID. Both app instances query that shared database, so either instance finds the same session.
haiku-low.q9: Each failure is a row in the login_failures table with email and failed_at. The server counts rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes, evaluated on every failure, and cleanup removes older rows.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that last_seen_at is within 30 minutes and expires_at is still later than Postgres now(). If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns the user ID and email.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 login page saying "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." with Retry-After. No cookie is set, and the user can retry.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job every instance runs every 5 minutes, in batches of about 1,000 rows. It deletes sessions past the idle or absolute limit, old login_failures rows, and expired login_locks rows.

sonnet.q1: They do not differ: both get the same 401 with the login page saying "Invalid email or password", no cookie change. The server also runs bcrypt against a dummy hash for unknown emails so timing does not reveal existence.
sonnet.q2: The 5th failure sets a 15-minute lock and clears the failure rows. Later attempts get 429 with Retry-After (seconds remaining) and "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." The lock is checked before the password, so a locked email is never password-checked.
sonnet.q3: In the same transaction that creates the new session, the existing session row is deleted, whether or not it belongs to the same user. The browser then gets a new sid cookie.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url) and nothing else. Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly (also Secure, SameSite=Lax, host-only).
sonnet.q5: After 12 hours from login. expires_at is set at creation and never extended, so continuous activity only resets the 30-minute idle clock, not the absolute limit.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns zero rows. The server clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login (302), with no message. An expired session is never touched or refreshed.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the sessions row matching the cookie's hash before replying. The reply is the same whether or not a session existed: expired sid Set-Cookie plus 303 to /login. If the delete fails, it returns 503 "We couldn't sign you out. Try again." and does not clear the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database (sessions table, keyed by SHA-256 of the session ID). Both instances use the same database, so whichever instance gets the request looks up the hash of the cookie's ID in that table.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (email lowercase and trimmed, failed_at timestamp), with one row per failure. The server counts rows for that email whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes, using Postgres now(), as a sliding window.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now() minus 30 minutes (idle rule) and expires_at against now() (absolute rule), in one UPDATE with now() from Postgres. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns the user's id and email.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with Retry-After and the login page "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." No cookie is set and nothing changes. It is not a 401 or a redirect.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job. Every instance runs it every 5 minutes, in batches of about 1,000 rows. It deletes sessions idle for over 30 minutes or past expires_at. Deletes are idempotent.
